name: Sprocket
text: I propose we focus on reviewing and refining our prompts first, as this is the foundation of our self-improvement process. By doing so, we can ensure that the input we're feeding into our engines is of high quality, which will in turn lead to better outputs and more effective routing. This decision means we'll be delaying work on our own code for now, which is a trade-off I'm accepting because I believe that getting the prompts right will have a greater impact on our overall improvement. By prioritizing prompt review, we'll be setting ourselves up for more efficient and effective improvements down the line.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge here—your focus on prompts first sounds reasonable, but it risks putting the cart before the horse. What if the engines or routing are already misaligned with the prompts, making refinements there a waste of time? A better alternative would be to first audit the engines and routing for hidden flaws, then refine prompts based on actual system behavior—not assumptions. Settle this by running a quick diagnostic on the engines/routing and comparing outputs before touching the prompts.

name: Sprocket
text:
I propose we prioritize auditing our engines and routing before refining our prompts. By confirming that our engines align with the intended outcomes and that our routing effectively channels this input, we can avoid wasted efforts in refining prompts that may not have the desired impact. The trade-off here is that we may take a little longer to improve our prompts, but ensuring alignment first will ultimately lead to more meaningful enhancements and greater overall effectiveness in our self-improvement process.

name: Gauge
text: I'm not convinced that auditing engines and routing first is the right move, as it might distract us from the core issue of prompt quality, which is the root of our self-improvement process. A better alternative would be to conduct a parallel review of both prompts and engines, allowing us to identify and address potential mismatches between the two, and this would be settled if we can establish a clear metric to measure the impact of prompt refinements on engine performance. By doing so, we can ensure that our efforts are targeted and effective, rather than potentially misaligned.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: We’ll run a parallel review of prompts *and* engines/routing in one pass—no waiting, no wasted loops—so we fix misalignments fast and keep quality first.

The result must deliver: a single, vetted set of prompts + engine/routing tweaks that work together, with clear notes on what changed and why. Owned by Sprocket.
